job_title: AI / ML & Full-Stack Software Engineer (Graduate / Entry-Level)
pool_summary: The contender pool clusters into three standout profiles: research-oriented AI builders with publications, advanced computer-vision or multimodal systems, and product-oriented engineers with measurable user or business outcomes. A smaller but meaningful group demonstrates retrieval-augmented generation, real-time architecture, international lab exposure, or open-source traction beyond ordinary coursework projects.

axes.label: Research-Grade AI Evidence
axes.rationale: Research outputs, externally funded work, and reproducible model evaluation distinguish candidates who can contribute to production AI beyond assembling standard demos. This axis separates genuine research depth from merely listing ML tools or completing an undifferentiated ML project.
axes.strong_criteria: Active ownership [action] of at least one peer-reviewed publication, externally funded research project, or research-grade AI system with a reported metric, novel method, or substantial experimental contribution; evidence should resemble the pool’s published work, funded segmentation research, or quantified model-building.
axes.moderate_criteria: Active ownership [action] of a substantive AI research or advanced model project without publication or external validation, or a clearly documented research internship contribution with a concrete dataset, model, or evaluation; peripheral participation in a research project is only moderate at most.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 7/30 candidates show strong or moderate evidence

axes.label: Multimodal Model-Building Depth
axes.rationale: The role spans LLMs, retrieval, computer vision, and predictive modeling, while the pool contains a selective set of candidates who built nontrivial systems across modalities rather than single-model classroom exercises. The differentiator is hands-on architecture and evaluation of complex AI systems, not baseline Python or ML exposure.
axes.strong_criteria: Active ownership [action] of a complex multimodal or advanced vision/NLP system using multiple model families, modalities, or stages, with a concrete evaluation result such as 82%+ accuracy/mIoU, OCR or ANPR performance, VQA, segmentation, or a comparable measured outcome.
axes.moderate_criteria: Active ownership [action] of one substantial computer-vision, NLP, recommendation, or predictive-modeling system using a nontrivial architecture such as CNNs, Transformers, BERT, CLIP, LSTM, or YOLO, but without multiple modalities, staged architecture, or a quantified evaluation; a simple classifier with a metric is moderate.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 9/30 candidates show strong or moderate evidence

axes.label: RAG Retrieval Architecture
axes.rationale: RAG is explicitly preferred for this role, but only a few candidates show exposure to the full retrieval mechanism rather than generic chatbot or LLM API usage. The key separation is active construction of hybrid retrieval and indexing pipelines with technically meaningful components and validation.
axes.strong_criteria: Active ownership [action] of an end-to-end RAG or semantic retrieval system combining at least two concrete mechanisms such as embeddings, BM25, FAISS, vector search, reranking, or domain-specific document retrieval, ideally with publication, evaluation, or a deployed workflow.
axes.moderate_criteria: Active ownership [action] of an LLM-powered assistant, semantic search, or document QA system using a single retrieval or model component, or peripheral contribution [peripheral] to a technically specified RAG pipeline such as embeddings/BM25/FAISS; generic ChatGPT API integration without retrieval is only moderate at most.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 4/30 candidates show strong or moderate evidence

axes.label: Quantified Product Impact
axes.rationale: Most candidates describe projects without adoption, business, or operational outcomes, whereas a small group demonstrates that their software changed engagement, retention, onboarding, usage, or processing performance. This axis is especially relevant to an applied AI and product-engineering role where prototypes must produce measurable user value.
axes.strong_criteria: Active ownership [action] of a shipped product or feature with at least one quantified outcome comparable to the pool’s evidence: roughly 30%+ improvement in engagement/satisfaction/retention, 25%+ reduction in onboarding, bounce, or inquiry burden, 50+ active users, 100+ daily users, or a similarly explicit business/usage metric.
axes.moderate_criteria: Active ownership [action] of a usable application with explicit but smaller-scale adoption, performance, or operational measurement, such as around 100 concurrent users, a quantified model/product result without clear business impact, or a concrete workflow improvement lacking a strong before-and-after metric.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 6/30 candidates show strong or moderate evidence

axes.label: Real-Time Full-Stack Architecture
axes.rationale: The full-stack portion of the role favors candidates who can integrate frontend, backend, persistence, authentication, and live communication rather than deliver isolated UI pages. Real-time messaging, WebSockets, WebRTC, and multi-layer application ownership form a selective architectural cluster in this pool.
axes.strong_criteria: Active ownership [action] of a multi-layer web or mobile application that integrates frontend and backend services, persistence/authentication, and real-time behavior through WebSockets, Socket.IO, WebRTC, or an equivalent mechanism, with explicit concurrency, usage, or production-scope evidence when available.
axes.moderate_criteria: Active ownership [action] of a complete frontend-backend application with database and API integration, or a real-time feature without demonstrated scale; isolated frontend work, a static website, or peripheral backend support is not strong and is moderate only when paired with meaningful application ownership.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 8/30 candidates show strong or moderate evidence
